mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS increase (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: In a robustness check, the interaction term (PAYEMS * -UNRATE) is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or explains less than 5% of the variance in 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy: GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-on-month growth rate > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically different from the 5-day return during a similar period of flat GDP growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound exceeding 2% in the same month suggests resolving supply bottlenecks, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-on-month decline > -5% followed by > 2% increase in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative when the INDPRO pattern is present (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for any consecutive three-month window, the market anticipates aggressive rate hikes, which compresses discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Inflation remains below 3% for the subsequent 6 months with no significant impact on 60-day forward returns (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for 4 consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS), suggests a tight labor market that fuels wage growth and equity valuations, yielding positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 4 consecutive months and PAYEMS < 200K for the same period
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS is not predictive of 20-day forward returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL accelerating), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days tend to be negative due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS month-on-month increase > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL month-on-month acceleration > 0.3%
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, the 5-day forward return is positive in > 40% of instances (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO) — a sharp drop followed by a smaller, sustained recovery — reduces uncertainty about supply constraints, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-on-month decline > -5% then a second consecutive month of > -2% growth
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative when the pattern is not detected (p > 0.05 in a t-test).
